# engram

> A single-binary terminal UI for the memories Claude Code writes to `~/.claude`,
> with team sharing over plain git. Free and open source under the MIT License.

Claude Code writes notes to itself as you work: what a project does, how you like
things, decisions you've made. They land as Markdown under `~/.claude`, one folder per project.
engram browses all of them in one two-pane TUI, and promotes the team-useful ones into a
git repository your teammates already have access to. No engram service or account:
your git host is the auth.

Claude Code shares team-written instructions through `CLAUDE.md` in the project repo,
but its auto-learned memories are machine-local. engram lets you promote selected
auto-learned memories through your own git remote.

- Install (Homebrew): `brew install ertugrulhaskan/tap/engram`
- Install (Go): `go install github.com/ertugrulhaskan/engram@latest`
- Platforms: macOS and Linux. Windows binaries ship but are untested; use WSL.
- Assistants: Claude Code, plus each project's `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md` and
  `.github/copilot-instructions.md` read-only — the instruction files Codex, Cursor, the
  Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot read. They are found for projects engram already tracks
  (those with a folder under `~/.claude/projects/`), and a `scanRoots` config setting points
  engram at any other folder, so a repo never opened in Claude Code appears too. The global
  `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` and `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` are listed as well, read straight from the
  home folder, and Cursor rules (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`) plus Copilot's path-scoped
  `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` list per project. No assistant exposes a memory
  API, so other sources arrive as local files first, export/import later.

- Team sharing: promote a memory — or several at once, marked with `space`, as a single
  commit and push — into a git store your team already has. A project-scoped memory is keyed
  to the git remote and lands in teammates' memory folders when they pull. A global-scoped one
  is tied to no repo: it lives in the store and keeps every copy you already hold in step, in
  whichever project you keep it. Every promoted memory is scanned for secrets first, including
  credentials broken across lines by a soft wrap or a YAML block scalar.
